title: Versatile Behavior Diffusion for Generalized Traffic Agent Simulation

control_signal.value: User requirement y at inference without retraining: goals or reference paths, soft constraints (speed limit, collision avoidance), behavior-prior (conflict-prior) selection, and game-theoretic cost objectives.

control_mechanism.value: Classifier-guidance-style conditional score: adds the gradient of the log-likelihood of y to the learned score during reverse diffusion, using model-based cost functions or predicted behavior priors as guidance.

base_model.value: Query-centric Transformer scene encoder, multi-modal marginal behavior predictor (static end-goal anchors), and a diffusion denoiser for joint multi-agent action trajectories under unicycle dynamics.

datasets.value: Waymo Open Motion Dataset (486,995 train, 44,097 validation scenarios; 44,920 Sim Agents test scenarios; 500 Validation Interactive scenarios for ablations), in Waymax closed-loop simulation.

metrics.value: Waymo Sim Agents benchmark; collision rate (%), off-road rate (%), ADE, FDE, minADE, minFDE, runtime (s) over 32 closed-loop samples.

controllability_evidence.value: Qualitative: conflict-prior guidance generates safety-critical scenarios from a model trained only on normal data (Fig. 8). No guided-control number appears in the packet.

stated_limitations.value: Conflict-prior guidance fails when behavior priors contain no collision pairs (shown as failure case). Future work: runtime efficiency for real-time use, LLM-based context-aware generation, other traffic domains.

notes: Guidance quantitative results (e.g. game-theoretic, goal reaching) are not in the packet, so the evidence field is qualitative.
